## The floor detector and the redo decision {#sec-ch08-redo}

### Summary

Everything else in this chapter keeps the state admissible or records that it could not. This is the
mechanism that decides the step was bad enough to take again, and it is the closest thing snapy has to a
positivity failure path.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Decide whether the step just taken must be redone: a floor test on the primitives plus the limiter marks.

**Data.** In: `hydro_u`, the floors, the two marks, the implicit clamp flag. Out: one boolean per block.

**Placement.** In `check_redo`, after the stages of a step and before the clock advances (@sec-ch01-driver).

**Activation.** Always; a hit is a primitive at or below $1.001$ times a floor, a NaN, a mark, or the clamp flag.

**Guarantee / limits.** Detection only: a redo repeats the step and the redo budget of @sec-ch07 ends the loop.

**Evidence.** `[C7]` of `floors_check`; the redo cases of `test_forcing.<b>`.
:::

### Derivation

The test is a margin above the floor rather than equality with it, at `hit`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::floor_hit >}}). A minimum density at or below $1.001$ times the
density floor counts as a hit. The same holds for pressure where there is a pressure row. Testing equality with the
floor would miss a cell that was floored and then nudged by a later operation; the margin catches the neighbourhood of
the floor instead. `[C7]` nudges a just-floored cell by fifteen relative amounts from $10^{-16}$ up to $10^{-3}$. The
margin counts all fifteen as hits. Equality counts only two, the unnudged cell and the single nudge below machine
epsilon, so thirteen are hits the margin keeps and equality loses. A density $1.002$ times the floor is a hit under
neither. `[C4]` covers the marking itself, including that it happens only from the interior [check
`src/snapy_report/ch08/checks/floors_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch08/checks/floors_check.out`].

Two orderings around it matter, and the code states both. In the decision the floor test runs first: it converts
the state to primitives to test them, and that conversion may itself make a limiter repair and set a mark. The marks
are read after the floor test, so that such a repair counts in this decision (`limiter_marks`,
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}). The marks are reset only later, in
`apply_redo`, once a redo has been decided and the state restored: the conversions of the floor test and of the
restore must not mark the step that is redone (`reset_limiter_marks`,
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}).

### Numerical method

The detector is `hydro_u` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::floor_hit >}}). The marks are read through
`limiter_hits` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::limiter_hits >}}), which returns the pair set by the
limiter passes of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter. The implicit clamp of @sec-ch08-vic is read through its own accessor at
`vic_dry_clamp_hit` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::vic_dry_clamp_hit >}}). The redo decision combines
them at {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}, where the floor test is run first
and the marks are read afterwards, so that a mark set by the floor test's own conversion is part of the decision.

**Why a margin, and why the marks are reset.** Three facts of the code.

1. The test is `!(min > 1.001 * floor)`, a margin above the floor rather than equality
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::floor_hit >}}). So a floored cell nudged by a later operation is
   still a hit. `[C7]` counts 15 of 15 nudges up to $10^{-3}$ relative, against 2 for equality.
2. The comparison is negated, so a NaN, which fails every comparison, counts as a hit.
3. The marks are read after the floor test, whose conversion may mark a repair that then counts in this decision
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}). They are reset in `apply_redo` after
   the redo is decided and the state restored, so the floor test's and the restore's conversions do not mark the
   redone step ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}).

: Code map of the floor detector. {#tbl-ch08-redo-code}

**How to use it.** Nothing is set; the detector reads the floors of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter. The floor test is
these lines ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::floor_hit >}}):

```cpp
  // negated so a NaN, which fails every comparison, counts as a hit
  bool hit = !(w[IDN].min().item<double>() > 1.001 * eos->density_floor());
  if (w.size(0) > IPR) {  // shallow water carries no pressure row
    hit = hit || !(w[IPR].min().item<double>() > 1.001 * eos->pressure_floor());
  }
  return hit;
```

`w` is the primitive state restored from `hydro_u` on the interior, and `eos` the equation-of-state options. A
driver sees the result as the positive return of `check_redo` and repeats the cycle (@sec-ch01-driver).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- A redo repeats the step; it does not make the step succeed. A column that floors at every step size
  will keep flooring, and the redo budget of the time-integration chapter is what ends the loop.
:::

1. **The margin is a constant.** The factor $1.001$ is not derived and not configurable. A cell
   legitimately sitting a tenth of a per cent above the floor is read as a hit.
2. **Detection is per block.** One floored cell marks the whole block for a redo, and nothing records
   which cell it was.
